title: Assessing Leukocyte-endothelial Interactions Under Flow Conditions in an Ex Vivo Autoperfused Microflow Chamber Assay
protocol: Connect 1 cm PE10 polyethylene tubing to 6 cm silicon tubing followed by 5 cm polyethylene tubing for the jugular side.
Prepare the carotid side similarly to the jugular side with the addition of a T-tube within the 6 cm silicon tubing about 1.5 cm away from the 1 cm polyethylene tubing.
Widen the silicon tube using fine forceps if necessary to insert the T-tube.
Connect one end of 10 cm silicone tubing to the pressure transducer.
Insert the T-end of the carotid side T-tube into the other end of the 10 cm silicone tubing.
Ensure that all connection sites are tight and leak free.
Apply a small rectangular piece of parafilm over where the tubing fits together, if necessary, to prevent leakage.
Prepare endothelial surface coating protein in 0.1% BSA, typically using 1 μg of protein per 200 μl for coating 4-5 chambers.
Infuse each chamber with endothelial surface coating protein using a 1 ml syringe connected to a 25 G needle.
Store the coated chambers in a 15 ml tube at 4 °C overnight.
Remove coated chambers from storage and connect jugular and carotid tubing to each side of the chamber.
Seal connections between tubing and chamber with parafilm stretched over the connection points.
Fill the chamber and tubing with 0.1% BSA using a syringe (check for leakage).
Incubate the chamber setup for 45 min at room temperature.
Cut notches on both sides of a 35 mm Petri dish to hold the chamber.
Stabilize the chamber in the prepared Petri dish by placing it in the cut notches.
Affix the chamber to the Petri dish using a small drop of silicone at the notched site.
Ensure the chamber is level under a microscope.
Allow silicone to dry for at least 15 min before further use.
Fill a 60 ml locking syringe with heparin and connect it to the pressure transducer.
Connect the pressure transducer to the carotid tubing in the following order: Transducer, silicon tubing, then T-tube.
Use a 1 cm PE50 between the silicon tubing connected to the transducer and the T-tube to secure the connection.
Pass the carotid artery silicon tubing through the pressure clamp.
Run 100USP heparin through the tubing and chamber until there are no air bubbles.
Turn on the computer, microscope, and open lab device.
Double click on the Leica application suite (or equivalent).
Prepare a folder to save the video: browse → acquire → movie → define sequence of clips (clips = 15, recording time = 30 sec, intervals = 15 sec) then click the “+” sign to confirm.
Coordinate the file name to the recording folder in step 4.1.
Anesthetize an 8-10 week-old mouse using a combination of ketamine (60 mg/kg) and xylazine (6 mg/kg) injected intra-peritoneally (IP).
Confirm that deep sedation is achieved within 5-10 min by loss of pedal withdrawal reflex.
If necessary, deliver isoflurane via face mask as needed to maintain proper anesthesia.
Place a warming pad under the cage and set to 37 °C to maintain body temperature.
Once proper anesthesia is confirmed, place the mouse in a ventral position.
Coat the eyes with bacitracin ointment to prevent ocular dryness.
Shave the hair at the incision site using a razor blade.
Thoroughly clean the site with alcohol.
Secure the animal with tape in a ventral position.
Expose the neck area and remove the thyroid gland to expose the trachea and vessels.
Clean the carotid artery until fully exposed, taking care not to damage the vagus nerve.
Fold a piece of suture and pass it underneath the carotid artery, then cut at the bend to create two pieces of suture underneath the carotid.
Loop each suture into knots without tightening them.
Repeat the procedure to expose the left jugular vein and prepare the sutures in the same manner.
Connect tubing to the mouse vasculature.
Inject 1 ml of heparin IP to heparinize the mouse.
Tighten the upper suture on the carotid artery.
Place the vessel clamp as low as it can go on the carotid artery.
Hold the artery by the upper suture with forceps and make a small incision, about 1/8 of the circumference of the artery.
Pass the carotid artery tubing through the second knot in the upper suture and into the incision made in the artery.
Tie off the lower suture to seal the artery around the tubing, making several knots for a tight seal.
Repeat the procedure for inserting the jugular vein tubing without using the vessel clamp.
Test the flow by releasing the vessel clamp.
Move the mouse to the microscope and connect the carotid tubing and jugular vein to the chamber tubing.
Open the carotid clamp to fill the chamber, creating a circuit with the mouse circulatory system.
Allow the blood to circulate for 3-5 minutes to stabilize flow conditions.
Adjust the microscope stage so that the chamber is level from one end to the other and parallel with the video recording window on the screen.
Fill the modified Petri dish containing the glass chamber with water.
Lower the 10X water immersion objective into the dish to make the cells flowing through the chamber visible.
Adjust the light intensity for adequate viewing of the cells, generally preferring a lower intensity.
Adjust the clamp on the tubing so that the transducer reads a steady 30 mm Hg, correlating to medium physiological flow pressure.
Press “start” to initiate recording both the video and the pressure starting near the jugular end and moving against the flow toward the carotid end until completed.
Close the valve at the input site to stop blood flow.
Remove the chamber from the circuit using fine forceps in one hand and grooved forceps in the other hand.
Fit a new chamber coated with a different adhesion molecule onto the circuit.
Resume recording for the new chamber as outlined in steps 6.1-6.4.
Euthanize all mice by CO2 asphyxiation followed by spinal cord dislocation at the end of the experiment.
Convert the recorded file to grayscale using ImageJ software by selecting File → Import → AVI and converting it to grayscale.
Standardize the frames in ImageJ by selecting Image → Property and entering the frame intervals globally.
Calculate the frame interval by dividing the total video duration (usually 30 seconds) by the number of frames in the video.
Measure the flow of each leukocyte using M TrackJ plugin: Add tracks, select a leukocyte, track it for 15-20 seconds with each frame, and merge.
Determine the mean rolling velocity of the leukocytes by selecting measure.
Copy all of the M TrakJ:Tracks into a spreadsheet.
Divide the values in the "mean V" column by 2/3 to convert into μm/sec.
Highlight and export pressure data into a spreadsheet.
Calculate ΔP (mm Hg) for each experimental group.
Calculate t (dyne/cm²) for each experimental group.
Copy calculated data into prism software for graphing.
